answer: Radio-range presence proofs. An identity registers only by answering a live challenge from three fixed beacons; measured round-trip times must match its claimed coordinates and a site-specific multipath fingerprint. A ridge, building, or shale bed alters that fingerprint, so replay from one radio fails. The rule rejects any two identities whose timing paths resolve to the same transceiver. Each identity therefore costs a powered transceiver physically placed at that site, plus calibration and maintenance; a single operator cannot fake two locations because light-speed timing would conflict.
